content.text:
<context query="Why Otto doesn't run on Cloud Run in europe-north1 as first planned" template="default" budget="8000">
<section name="Conventions" source="repo" priority="1">
<document source="specs/support-agent-deployment/spec.md" type="spec" relevance="1.00" tokens="2956">
## Dependencies and Open Questions

- **The repo deploys differently from every issue in this feature.** The issues assume Google Cloud Run in `europe-north1`, with terraform under `infrastructure/terraform/` (`shared/`, `environments/poc/`, `access/`, `bootstrap/`) and a `deploy-poc.yaml` workflow. The repo deploys to GKE with Helm in `europe-west1`:
  - The `deploy` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `helm upgrade --install` of `charts/otto` with `deploy/recinq-test.values.yaml` onto the GKE Autopilot cluster `n8n-cluster` in project `re5-n8n-platform`, region `europe-west1`, namespace `otto`. Images go to `ghcr.io/re-cinq/otto-api` and `ghcr.io/re-cinq/otto-web` (the `images` job), not Artifact Registry. There are no Cloud Run services, no `gcloud run deploy` line and no `deploy-poc.yaml`.
  - Terraform lives in `infra/terraform`: the reusable `modules/otto-deployer` and the `recinq-test` root, which sets `region = "europe-west1"`, so FR-074 as written would fail against today's tree. There is no `shared/`, `environments/poc/` or `bootstrap/` root. #161's access root sits at `infra/terraform/access/`, planned and applied by `.github/workflows/terraform-access.yml` as the identities of `infra/terraform/modules/otto-access-identity`, which `recinq-test` applies; its one project is `re5-n8n-platform`, standing in for both the `poc` and the shared project. The `recinq-test` root is applied by hand by "someone who can manage IAM in the project and RBAC in the cluster" (`README.md`); no workflow applies terraform, and CI only runs `fmt` and `validate` (the `terraform` job in `ci.yml`).
  - `re5-n8n-platform` is shared with Lore's cluster, not a dedicated `poc` project, so a human binding there reaches more than Otto. Which project's log bucket receives the api's logs on the shared cluster is not recorded in the repo.
  - The only `backend "gcs"` block is in `infra/terraform/recinq-test/main.tf`: `bucket = "re5-n8n-terraform-state"`, `prefix = "otto"`. That bucket belongs to the shared project, was not created by this repository, and its location is stated nowhere in the repo; if it is not in `europe-north1`, FR-064's migration branch applies to it. That root writes `github_actions_secret` values into state (the WIF provider path and the deployer service account email, not secret payloads); `README.md` records that `LORE_INGEST_TOKEN` is kept out of Terraform on purpose.
  - Today's bindings are all machine bindings, in `infra/terraform/modules/otto-deployer/main.tf`: `roles/container.clusterViewer` on the project for `otto-deployer`, `roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser` on that account for one GitHub subject (a push to Otto's `main`), and a Kubernetes `admin` RoleBinding in the `otto` namespace. `infra/terraform/modules/otto-runtime-identity/main.tf` (#253) adds the second machine identity: `roles/aiplatform.user` for `otto-api-runtime`, and `roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser` on that account for the `otto/otto-api` Kubernetes service account alone.
  - Parts of the intent have a GKE counterpart that does not satisfy the Cloud Run wording: one api instance (`charts/otto/templates/api-deployment.yaml` refuses any `api.replicaCount` other than 1); the one-hour socket (`deploy/recinq-test.values.yaml` sets the nginx ingress `proxy-read-timeout` and `proxy-send-timeout` to `3600`); log level (`charts/otto/values.yaml` sets `api.logLevel: info`); non-root (the root `Dockerfile`'s `api` stage runs `USER 1000` on `node:22-slim`); reviewable instance count, resources, probes and security context (`charts/otto/values.yaml`, `charts/otto/templates/api-deployment.yaml`), with public reach as the ingress in `deploy/recinq-test.values.yaml`; and the same writer split, since CI sets only `api.image.tag` and `web.image.tag` on the command line. Health is checked only by a curl of `https://otto.gcp.re-cinq.com/api/health` in the `deploy` job; there is no WebSocket smoke step.
  - Whether the re:cinq test environment is a precursor to this deployment or replaces it is not recorded anywhere. The requirements stay Cloud Run in `europe-north1`.
- CI posture today: every `uses:` in `ci.yml` is SHA-pinned, every checkout sets `persist-credentials: false`, and the `deploy` job holds `contents: read, id-token: write` at job level. The `npm ci --ignore-scripts` conflict is recorded under Reconciled Decisions.
- `adrs/ADR-003-hosting-and-data-residency.md` records the residency of the GKE deployment (#414); #27's `docs/adr/ADR-001-hosting-platform.md` was never written. `docs/access.md` and `scripts/check-deploy-invariants.ts` exist with #161's human-binding half only. None of `docs/poc-operating-limits.md`, `docs/deployment.md` or `apps/api/src/http/denyChatRoutes.ts` exists. `CORS_ORIGIN` and `VITE_HAL_WS_URL` are read nowhere; the chart passes only `API_PORT`, `API_BASE_PATH` and `LOG_LEVEL` to the api container.
- **Blocked (#161).** `KU-30` has not recorded who may read a customer's conversation. The access root, the check and the workflow are built and tested against a placeholder list now; the real names are the last commit. `user:` only also avoids depending on whether a Cloud Identity or Workspace directory exists, which `KU-30` leaves unresolved.
- The org's existing terraform applies on release, which would leave a removed member's access live until the next release cut. That is why access changes get their own push trigger.
- The org's only existing bootstrap precedent grants `storage.objectAdmin` only, which lacks `buckets.get` and would leave the drift plan reader unable to read the state bucket's location. That is why FR-068 and FR-069 grant a bucket-reading role. [compliance-drift-checks](../compliance-drift-checks/spec.md) (#45) separately binds its state reader to `roles/storage.objectViewer` in `drift-reader.tf`; which of the two grants that reader relies on for the location is not stated in either issue.
- `planDrift`, `compliance/hosting-baseline.json` and the human-IAM reader come from [compliance-drift-checks](../compliance-drift-checks/spec.md) (#45); FR-018, FR-019, CR-009 and CR-010 wait on it.
- The deployment is verifiable today without a model decision: the `MODEL_ID` fallback of [support-agent-prompt-and-model](../support-agent-prompt-and-model/spec.md) (#22) and the fixtures of [support-agent-tms-tools](../support-agent-tms-tools/spec.md) (#17) cover it.
- FR-005's "every in-process store is only truthful at one instance" is one of the readings behind the one-replica guard recorded as Open in [support-agent-conversation-data](../support-agent-conversation-data/spec.md).
- [support-agent-operations-security](../support-agent-operations-security/spec.md) (#42, #165, #202) builds on this deployment: the advisory route verifies its deployed digest, the alerts live in its `poc` root, and the build-chain audit runs before its image build.
- **Settled on documentation, not on a live cluster (#253): `automountServiceAccountToken` stays `false`.** Google's Workload Identity Federation for GKE credential flow is: "Application default credentials (ADC) requests a Google Cloud access token from the Compute Engine metadata server that runs on the VM. The GKE metadata server intercepts the token request and asks the Kubernetes API server for a Kubernetes ServiceAccount token that identifies the requesting workload. This credential is a JSON web token (JWT) that's signed by the API server. The GKE metadata server uses Security Token Service to exchange the JWT for a short-lived federated access token" (<https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/concepts/workload-identity>, "Credential flow", read 2026-09-23). The metadata server, a DaemonSet on every node, fetches that token itself; nothing in the pod reads it off a projected volume, so `automountServiceAccountToken: false` does not break the exchange, and what does decide the pod's identity is `serviceAccountName`. The how-to page adds that "Existing code that authenticates using the instance metadata server (like code using the Google Cloud client libraries) should work without modification" (<https://docs.cloud.google.com/kubernetes-engine/docs/how-to/workload-identity>), which covers `@google-cloud/vertexai` and, from HAL Engine 0.8.0, `@google/genai`, both authenticating through Google's auth library. This corrects [support-agent-prompt-and-model](../support-agent-prompt-and-model/spec.md)'s reading that Workload Identity hands ADC the projected token, and the matching comment in `deploy/recinq-test.values.yaml`. **Not tested against the cluster.** No apply was run, the account does not exist yet, and the only kubectl context available while writing this is a local minikube, not `n8n-cluster`. The proof is the change that sets `api.modelId` and watches the api answer.

# Support agent deployment

| Field     | Value                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Feature   | Support agent deployment                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Issue     | re-cinq/Otto#27, #161, #162, #168, #253                                                                                                                                                               |
| Status    | Draft                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Created   | 2026-09-11                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Epic      | E4 - OLT support agent                                                                                                                                                                                |
| Milestone | M2 - PoC on fixtures (#27, #161, #162, #253); M4 - Production readiness (#168)                                                                                                                        |
| Builds on | [support-agent-foundation](../support-agent-foundation/spec.md) (#13), [support-agent-chat](../support-agent-chat/spec.md) (#14), [compliance-drift-checks](../compliance-drift-checks/spec.md) (#45) |
| Blocked   | #161 (KU-30: who may read a customer's conversation is not recorded; the access root, check and workflow are built against a placeholder list and the names are the last commit)                      |

This feature puts the support agent on a URL OLT can use and makes every fact about where it runs and who can reach it a reviewed file. It planned two Google Cloud Run services in `europe-north1`, declared as terraform resources in a `poc` root, with CI writing only the image. That plan (#27, #162, #168) is superseded: Otto deploys with Helm to GKE in `europe-west1`, and `adrs/ADR-003-hosting-and-data-residency.md` records the platform as deployed and a residency table for every place a customer's question rests or passes through (#414). Human access to the projects lives in its own terraform root, applied on merge, so revoking someone is a pull request. One invariants script keeps the region, the timeouts, the deploy flags, the human bindings and the state bucket from drifting, and a post-deploy smoke step proves a real conversation streams end to end.
</document>
</section>
<section name="Architecture Decisions" source="adrs" priority="2">
<document source="adrs/ADR-003-hosting-and-data-residency.md" type="adr" relevance="1.00" tokens="560">
## Context

OLT delegated the platform choice to re:cinq on one condition: the client must know where its data is, fully documented and NIS-2 compliant, because OLT operates in critical infrastructure. In OLT's words, re:cinq must be able to document and prove that data does not leave the controlled hosting environment.

#27 planned Google Cloud Run in `europe-north1`, to sit "in the same region as the Vertex model", and a residency table in `docs/adr/ADR-001-hosting-platform.md`. Neither was built. Otto deploys to the shared GKE cluster instead ([support-agent-deployment](../specs/support-agent-deployment/spec.md) records the divergence), and the premise of the region choice is gone. Measured on 2026-10-16, `europe-north1` serves only the Gemini 2.5 family, which Google retires on 2026-10-20, and the newer Gemini models answer only on the `eu` multi-region ([support-agent-prompt-and-model](../specs/support-agent-prompt-and-model/spec.md), "Region availability, measured"). #27, #162 and #168 are closed as superseded. ADR-001 is the TMS authentication decision (#15), so this record is ADR-003.

# ADR-003: Hosting and data residency

| Field      | Value                                                                                                       |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Status     | Accepted                                                                                                    |
| Decided    | 2026-10-19                                                                                                  |
| Decides    | Where Otto runs, and where a support conversation rests or passes through (#414)                            |
| Supersedes | The `docs/adr/ADR-001-hosting-platform.md` that #27 planned for Cloud Run in `europe-north1`, never written |

## Rejected alternatives

- **Cloud Run in `europe-north1` (#27).** It rested on the model running in `europe-north1`, which no current Gemini model does, and on terraform roots this repository never built.
- **The model's `global` endpoint.** It runs every Gemini model but gives up the EU residency the model allowlist exists to enforce.
</document>
</section>

</document>

content.text: {"answer": "Otto deploys with Helm to the shared GKE Autopilot cluster `n8n-cluster` in `europe-west1`, so the Cloud Run plan in `europe-north1` (issue #27) was never built. ADR-003 (decided 2026-10-19) says the region choice rested on the model running in `europe-north1`, 'in the same region as the Vertex model'. That premise no longer holds. Measured on 2026-10-16, `europe-north1` serves only the Gemini 2.5 family, which Google retires on 2026-10-20. The newer Gemini models answer only on the `eu` multi-region. The ADR lists Cloud Run in `europe-north1` under 'Rejected alternatives'. It says the plan rested on that model-region assumption and on terraform roots (`shared/`, `environments/poc/`, `bootstrap/`, a `deploy-poc.yaml` workflow) that the repo never built. The ADR also rejects the model's `global` endpoint, because it gives up the EU residency the model allowlist exists to enforce. Issues #27, #162 and #168 were closed as superseded. The planned `docs/adr/ADR-001-hosting-platform.md` was never written, and ADR-003 replaces it.", "sources": ["adrs/ADR-003-hosting-and-data-residency.md", "specs/support-agent-deployment/spec.md", "specs/support-agent-prompt-and-model/spec.md (Region availability, measured)"]}
